title: Cents and Sensibility with Ronnie Delacroix
description: Late-night money advice on Snazzie FM. Listeners write in with real debt and savings troubles. Ronnie answers every single one by telling them to open another credit card. Barry tries to slip in a real number. It does not go well.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to Cents and Sensibility, the only money show that believes in you. I'm Ronnie Delacroix. That's my co-host Barry, and tonight, friends, we are taking your real financial troubles.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: And, just to say up front, I am a little nervous about the format this week.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Don't be nervous, Barry. Money is simple. Let's get into the mailbag.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: First one. Diane from the east side, who emailed us. She writes, quote, I am forty-one thousand dollars deep across four credit cards, the minimum payments alone eat my whole paycheck, and I just want a realistic plan to start digging out. Unquote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, so that's serious. The first real move there is the highest interest card, you list them, you attack the worst rate first...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Diane, first of all, congratulations. Four approvals? Look at that credit history. The banks LOVE you. So here's what we do, sweetheart. We consolidate. You open one more card, a fifth, and you pay the four with it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's, that's a fifth card. That's just five cards.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Four plus one is fewer, Barry. Mathematically. <p:0.3> Because now it's one decision.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not how either of those words works.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Next letter. Now this one Barry's going to read, it came in as a voicemail. Go ahead, Barry.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Right. This is Marcus. He says, quote, I'm twenty-six, I finally want to start saving for a house, I've got about three hundred dollars left over each month, and I just want to know where a normal person should even put it. Unquote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Beautiful question, Marcus. So forget saving. You want to invest in yourself. <p:0.3> Buy a boat.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A boat. He has three hundred dollars and he wants a house.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A boat IS a house, Barry. A house that appreciates. And then you rent it out.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: To who? Rent it to who?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: To the ocean.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's the ocean, Ronnie. The ocean does not pay rent.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Untapped market, Barry. <p:0.3> Moving on.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now this next one is from Carol, who writes in every week, God love her. She says, quote, my mother passed, and the funeral home wants eight thousand dollars I do not have, I'm grieving and I'm panicking and I just need to know my options. Unquote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Oh, Carol. I'm so sorry. Ronnie, this one we just be human about, okay?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Carol, my deepest condolences. Truly. <p:0.3> And speaking of lasting memories, tonight's show is brought to you by Eternal Stay mattresses, you'll sleep like the dead.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. Ronnie, no.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now, Carol, here's the move. You open a card in your mother's honor. She'd want the points.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You... you cannot open a credit card for a deceased person, Ronnie. That's, that's a crime.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And THAT, Barry, is exactly the kind of small thinking that keeps people in debt.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Okay, this next one came in as a complaint, but I'm choosing to read it as fan mail. It's from Winston. He writes, quote, I am a credentialed financial planner, and I am begging you, on behalf of my entire profession, to stop telling people to open credit cards. Three things you said last week were technically illegal. Unquote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: See, an actual professional is telling you the same thing I'm telling you...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Winston, thank you. Truly. The kind words mean everything.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Those were not kind words. He listed crimes, Ronnie. He listed three crimes.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You know what I think the problem is, Winston? I think YOU'RE the one carrying tension. Me? I have nine cards. Maybe eleven. <p:0.3> And I have never once felt richer.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So, Winston, my friend. Have you considered consolidating?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry's gone quiet, folks. He does that.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Last one tonight. And I want to be clear up front, this is from a young man named Trevor, who has no debt. He writes, quote, I saved diligently, I paid cash for everything, I owe nothing to anyone, and I just wanted to share a rare good-news money story with the show. Unquote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's wonderful. That's, honestly, that's the only healthy letter we've had all night. Just say nice job, Trevor.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry. Barry, this is the scariest letter we've read.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: What? He has zero debt. That's the goal. That's the whole goal.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A man with no debt has no relationships with banks, Barry. He's a ghost. He doesn't exist. Trevor, you need to open a card TONIGHT.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He doesn't need an emergency fund, he doesn't have an emergency!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: An emergency fund is just an emergency with a number on the front, Barry. <p:0.3> Trevor, consolidate the nothing into something. Open the card. Be real.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: And finally, a quick update. From Diane. The listener from segment one. She took your advice.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She writes, quote, I now have five cards. <p:0.3> And a sixth card I opened to pay the annual fee on the fifth. Unquote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Six decisions down to one. <p:0.3> That's the Cents and Sensibility difference, folks. Sleep tight.
